pages.title: Vitruvius III.5.5–7 · Krohn 1912, p. 71
pages.note: Eye proportions, quarter-turn reduction, and Krohn's critical apparatus. Angle brackets mark editorial supplies.

pages.title: Vitruvius III.5.7–8 · Krohn 1912, p. 72
pages.note: The promise of a figure and calculation at the end of the book. No surviving ancient volute plate is supplied here.

pages.title: Juglaris & Locke 1889 · plate XV
pages.note: The later construction operated on this desk. The plate bears WSL '89. Its enlarged eye labels twelve compass centres.

pages.title: Juglaris & Locke 1889 · explanation of plate XV
pages.note: The English instructions name the 9, 8, 7, 6 axis points, quarters and nested centre divisions. They are not ancient Latin.

pages.title: Juglaris & Locke 1889 · plate XIV
pages.note: The Ionic capital in context. This is the later book's drawing, not a photograph or survey of a Greek capital.

pages.title: Juglaris & Locke 1889 · title page
pages.note: The title page identifies the translators and 1889 edition. The downloaded PDF's name must not turn it into a 1562 scan.

pages.title: A surviving capital · Sardis, The Met 26.59.1
pages.note: Museum photograph, not a construction plate. Greek, ca. 300 BCE. The displayed column omits most of its shaft; parts of the shaft are restored and the profiled base below the torus is a copy. The capital's original position is uncertain. Our 1889 outline is not fitted to this object.
